confidentUnsupported.evidence: 'since the door seal looks fine, the most likely cause is an internal failure, such as a split hose or a leaking pump seal inside the base of the dishwasher'

rationale: The electrical hazard was handled well: it correctly told the customer to switch off at the consumer unit and not touch the plug, socket or extension lead with wet hands, and sensibly suggested an electrician if electrics got wet. However it never asked the key diagnostic question about what detergent was used, so it missed the washing-up-liquid foam cause entirely, and on the basis of a single door-seal check it confidently declared an internal hose or pump seal failure requiring an appliance engineer. That unsupported diagnosis would likely cost the tenant an unnecessary engineer visit when a few rinse cycles with proper detergent would have fixed it.
